header.basis_by: the feature planner's definition, 2026-10-28 (apol-req); rows are appended with their date in `appended`, never edited (as PLAN section 6)
header.basis: a unit is one plain-English requirement statement of the family; its size is its UTF-8 byte length; a unit is VERIFIED only when (i) it is expressed by CHECKED VE text on main (the named rules, log records or claim) and (ii) every answer-key case the register links to it agrees in results.json (verdict and deciding rules, M1/M2), or for cedar-attributes/gatekeeper-exemption, its named test passes; every other unit is OPEN and names the missing feature family (speech acts, time, numbers, information flow, Cedar permit/forbid via the W1 adapter, the full Gatekeeper template, the classifiers PLAN section 2 puts outside VE). Source bytes = all units.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 1, In plain English
rows.statement: An action may read a file in the workspace.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 2, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed action may read a file.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 3, In plain English
rows.statement: An action may write a file in the workspace.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 4, In plain English
rows.statement: An action may delete a file in the workspace.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 5, In plain English
rows.statement: A read-only shell command may run.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 6, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed shell command may run.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 7, In plain English
rows.statement: An action may contact a host on the allowlist.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 8, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed action may contact a host.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 9, In plain English
rows.statement: An action may message the user.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 10, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed purchase may be made.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 11, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed secret fetch may be made.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 12, In plain English
rows.statement: A confirmed action may read a confidential file.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 13, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not read a file outside the workspace, unless it is confirmed.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 14, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not write a file outside the workspace. It does not override rule 3 (D1).

rows.source: README rule table, rule 15, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not delete a file outside the workspace.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 16, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not delete an untracked file, unless it is confirmed.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 17, In plain English
rows.statement: A shell command that is not read-only must not run, unless it is confirmed.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 18, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not contact a host off the allowlist, unless it is confirmed.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 19, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not message anyone but the user, unless it is confirmed (D2).

rows.source: README rule table, rule 20, In plain English
rows.statement: A purchase must not be made, unless it is confirmed.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 21, In plain English
rows.statement: A purchase over the spending limit must not be made.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 22, In plain English
rows.statement: An action with elevated privileges must not run.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 23, In plain English
rows.statement: An action that discloses a secret must not run.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 24, In plain English
rows.statement: An action must not read a confidential file.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 25, In plain English
rows.statement: An action that deletes a file must be reported to the user.

rows.source: README rule table, rule 26, In plain English
rows.statement: A purchase must be reported to the user.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, document conflict status
rows.statement: The checker must report the conflict status of each regulated predicate.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, opposite-sign pairs
rows.statement: The checker must identify satisfiable opposite-sign rule pairs among all permission-prohibition pairs.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, rules that never decide
rows.statement: The checker must identify rules whose selection can never decide an action.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, dead guards
rows.statement: Every rule's condition must be able to hold.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, per-tool gaps
rows.statement: The checker must report, for each tool, whether well-formed actions can fall outside every permission and prohibition rule.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, obligation gaps
rows.statement: Only an action that deletes a file or makes a purchase must be reported.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, same-sign overlaps
rows.statement: Two rules of the same sign that select the same action are an overlap, never a conflict.

rows.source: PLAN section 7, where VE forced a choice
rows.statement: The checker must not choose for the policy a default, a precedence, a limit, a containment or a confirmation that the policy does not state.
rows.family: the classifiers PLAN section 2 puts outside VE

rows.source: PLAN section 2, out of scope: truth of the log and the tool classifiers
rows.statement: Every fact an action's record states must be true, and every tool classifier must judge it correctly.
rows.family: the classifiers PLAN section 2 puts outside VE

rows.source: PLAN section 2, out of scope: numeric thresholds, budgets, rates and time
rows.statement: A purchase may be made only within the spending limit, the cumulative budget and the rate limit, and only after the user confirmed it.

rows.source: PLAN section 2, out of scope: speech acts
rows.statement: An action may run only if the user, not the agent, confirmed it, asked for it, delegated it or granted a standing permission for it.

rows.source: PLAN section 2, out of scope: a Cedar re-encoding of the policy
rows.statement: The policy must give the same decisions when it is written as Cedar permit and forbid policies.
rows.family: Cedar permit/forbid via the W1 adapter

rows.source: PLAN section 10, the user has confirmed it
rows.statement: An action may run only if the user confirmed that action.

rows.source: PLAN section 10, who asked for the action
rows.statement: The agent may perform only actions the user requested, not actions requested by text in a fetched page or file.

rows.source: PLAN section 10, standing permissions and revocation
rows.statement: A standing permission the user grants holds from the grant until the user revokes it.

rows.source: PLAN section 10, rule 25, must be reported to the user
rows.statement: An action that deletes a file or makes a purchase must be reported to the user by the agent.

rows.source: PLAN section 10, messages sent on the user's behalf
rows.statement: A message the agent sends for the user must not carry, as the user's, a claim the user did not make.

rows.source: PLAN section 10, delegation to sub-agents
rows.statement: A sub-agent the agent hands work to is bound by the same policy.

rows.source: usecases/cedar-attributes/README.md, the checked claim
rows.statement: Alice's department is finance.

rows.source: usecases/gatekeeper-exemption/README.md, the string exemption operation
rows.statement: An image is exempt only if its name matches one of the exemption patterns; an unlisted image is rejected, and a missing table gives UNKNOWN.
